title: mantissa-first-fp8-delta-compact-probe-for-kv-cache
creator: Anika Patel
description: Experiment to evaluate a mantissa-first FP8 + delta residual compression pipeline for KV cache entries to reduce GPU memory footprint without materially degrading generation quality. This probe targets hot-serving paths during continuous batching where KV dominates working set size for long-context models (32k+). We compare: mantissa-only FP8, FP8 with per-chunk bias compensation, INT8 asymmetric quant, and an aggressive INT4 tiled fallback. Measure quality (LM loss/perplexity, token-level error, targeted eval prompts), end-to-end latency change under continuous batching, and effective GPU memory reduction at model scales 7B/13B/70B across sequence lengths 4k/16k/32k.
acceptance_criteria: Achieve >=45% average KV memory reduction vs baseline FP32 for 16k+ contexts on 13B with <=1.0% relative perplexity regression on evaluation suite
P99 token generation latency increase <=10ms under baseline batching profile (batch size distribution recorded in benchmark plan)
Runtime can automatically detect and fallback to higher-fidelity mode per-request if quality regressions exceed thresholds
Experiment produces reproducible benchmark scripts and a single confluence doc with results and recommended config knobs
experiment_steps: Implement mantissa-only FP8 serializer for KV tensors: store 6-bit mantissa with shared exponent per 64-token chunk; integrate per-chunk bias residual stored as int8 delta
Add lightweight calibration pass that samples warm-up requests to compute chunk exponents and residual scale factors; offline path and fast online estimator
Integrate tiled INT4 packing path as an emergency low-memory mode with higher reconstruction overhead and per-layer error-correction lookup
Hook compressor into runtime KV write path with A/B flagging and metrics tracing (per-token reconstruction error distribution, compress ratio, encode/decode microsecond cost)
Run controlled offline experiments across model sizes with fixed prompt set (internal bench harness) to log perplexity, micro-F1 on QA probes, and generation regressions
Deploy to canary cluster behind feature flag and run production shadow traffic for 48 hours to detect rare failure modes
Collect telemetry and run cohort analysis: tail error patterns, prompt-length sensitivity, decoder step-wise error accumulation
Draft recommendation: default config (mantissa-FP8) + fallback thresholds + knobs for Dedicated plans
notes: Rationale: previous experiments focused on block-wise integer quant; mantissa-first FP8 may preserve dynamic range for attention KV while enabling better residual compaction for long contexts

Trade-offs: mantissa-first reduces storage but requires chunk-level exponent sync; risk of step-wise error accumulation across autoregressive decode which we mitigate via occasional full-precision checkpoints in KV cache
Fallback policy: if cumulative token-level reconstruction error > threshold or generation divergence detected, runtime will keep raw FP32 for that sequence and mark encoder bucket as high-fidelity
Perf expectations: encode/decode should add ~2-7us per KV write/read on A100; memory reduction target 40-60% depending on model and context length
Cross-team: coordinate with Serving Runtime (kernel selection) and Console (observability events + rollout UI) for rollout and metric capture
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: subtle downstream quality regressions not visible in aggregate perplexity. Mitigation: include targeted adversarial prompt set and human review for top regressions
Risk: added latency for small-batch low-latency tier. Mitigation: disable compression for latency-sensitive routes and provide explicit routing flag
Risk: exponent drift across distributed KV shards. Mitigation: encode absolute chunk metadata and version tokens; include compatibility header to allow mixed-precision reads
metrics_to_capture: KV memory bytes per active sequence (mean/p50/p95/p99)
Perplexity delta vs FP32 baseline on evaluation corpus
Token reconstruction MSE and max-abs error distributions per layer
End-to-end P50/P90/P99 token generation latency under continuous batching workload
Fallback rate and reasons (quality vs decode error vs telemetry mismatch)
